instructions: Up to 4 days ahead, heat the oven to 375°F. Set the pie crust on the counter to thaw while the oven heats, about 10 minutes.
Cut 2 cups of small florets from the broccoli.
Put the florets in a small pot with about 1 cup of water. Cover and bring it to a boil, then cook for about 4 minutes, until they're bright green and tender but still have some bite.
Drain the broccoli in a colander, rinse it with cool water and drain it again. Chop it into small pieces.
In a large bowl, whisk the 5 eggs, 3/4 cup milk, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper until there are no streaks of white left.
Stir in the broccoli and 1 cup of the cheddar. Pour it into the pie crust.

Set the quiche on a baking sheet and bake for 35 to 50 minutes, until the center is set and a knife near the middle comes out clean. Start checking at 25 minutes, and cover the edge with foil if the crust browns too fast.
Let it stand for 5 minutes, then cut it into 8 slices. This makes 8 slices.

Once it's cool, the slices keep in the fridge for up to 4 days, wrapped, or in the freezer for up to 3 months. In the morning, microwave a slice for about 1 minute, or warm it in a 350°F oven for about 10 minutes.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the quiche up to 4 days ahead and keep the slices in the fridge.
method_notes: All three bake 5 eggs with milk or cream, broccoli and sharp cheddar in a 9 inch crust until the center is set. Kristine's Kitchen (the lead) keeps it to five ingredients: blanched, chopped broccoli and cheddar stirred into the eggs and poured into an unbaked deep-dish crust at 375°F. Well Plated blind bakes the crust and sautés the broccoli with green onions and adds Parmesan, and Inspired Taste uses cream, onion, garlic and a blind-baked butter crust baked low and slow. This one follows the lead with a store-bought frozen crust, and the 4 day fridge time comes from Inspired Taste.
